It runs under `afk-python` directly (no shell) and reads the provider declarations in `hooks/lib/providers/<name>.json`. It judges the resource a call mutates (the main checkout, a protected branch's worktree, a worktree another live session holds) and allows everything else, composed commands and unknown programs included (ADR-0010). It snapshots guarded checkouts before an allowed shell call. It fails closed inside a work tree (20 s deadline, under the 30 s hook timeout). Placement comes from the file layout; one `git rev-parse` covers unusual layouts. Protection comes from `scripts/protected-lookup.py`, which reuses a forge answer for at most 5 minutes (`AFK_PROTECTION_CACHE_TTL`; never for the default branch, `main` or `master`). A refusal is exit 0 plus the deny JSON, never exit 2: the H-2 harness runs the command when a hook exits 2. Bypass: `AFK_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1` set by a human at launch. The same process runs the **lavish rule** (`lib/lavish_direct.py`) first: a shell call that runs `lavish-axi` in executable position (bare, by path or `.cmd`/`.ps1` shim, behind `env`/`command`/`exec`/`npx`, or inside `bash -c`/`pwsh -Command` or a double-quoted `$(…)`) or sets `LAVISH_AXI_HOST` is denied with the `scripts/lavish_show.py` command; searches, mentions, comments, `declare -p`, `lavish-axi --version` and unreadable shell syntax pass, and `AFK_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1` does not lift it (`LAVISH.md` "Pin and invocation"). Rule: `SAFETY.md` "Worktree per session".

Seam 1: project_from_remote.project() strips the scheme, the user and the host and returns only the path (owner/name); it never returns a host, so the helper cannot take the host from it.

Seam 1: four callers rely on the owner/name-only return of project(): github forge.sh:139 (--repo), gitlab forge.sh:147 (-R), afk-config.py repo_slug (keeps a one-slash path only) and protected-lookup.py facts(); widening the return to carry a host would break all four and turn test_project_from_remote red.

Seam 1/3: host derivation already exists twice: scripts/protected-lookup.py facts() returns forge, repo, host and remote (_host_of(url), re-resolved through git for insteadOf and include), and adapters/forge/branch_protection.py _hostname() maps a host to a CLI-logged-in host, resolving an SSH alias with ssh -G. A new helper that re-derives the host restates that fact (AGENTS.md DRY rule).

Seam 1: forge.sh knows the remote only when github.remote or gitlab.remote is set; otherwise resolve_repo returns empty, REPO_FLAG stays empty and the CLI derives the project from the checkout itself.

Seam 1: with no *.remote set, a helper that picks a remote for the host (protected-lookup picks the branch's remote) can pick a different remote than gh or glab picks for the project, so host and project can disagree.

Seam 1: the AFK_CFG view already carries developer.* keys from every layer, the shared overlay included: load() deep-merges home, repo, shared overlay, local and AFK_CONFIG, and export_shell flattens every loaded key; developer.forgeAccount would export as AFK_CFG_DEVELOPER_FORGEACCOUNT (shell_name uppercases, no camelCase split).
Seam 1: forgeAccount is in neither DEVELOPER_KEYS (afk-config.py:73) nor CONFIG.md's developer schema row (CONFIG.md:136).

Seam 1: an unknown developer key fails `afk-config.py validate` (developer.forgeAccount: unknown key, exit 2) but export-shell never validates, so afk_config_load still exports it; `afk-config.py resolve forgeAccount` exits 2 until the key joins DEVELOPER_KEYS.

Seam 1/3: adding forgeAccount to DEVELOPER_KEYS turns two tests red unless the same commit updates CONFIG.md (test_afk_config.py:357 compares it with CHILD_KEYS) and skills/afk/setup/scripts/developer_values.py ORDER (test_setup_developer_values.py:167).

Seam 2: forge.sh runs in its own process and reloads the configuration each run (AFK_CFG_* are plain assignments, not exported), and the ledger reaches it as bash -c '. adapter.sh; afk_adapter forge "$1"' in its own cwd, so an account set for a repository applies to every ledger call there.
Seam 2: every gh call in github forge.sh goes through gh(), the `"${create[@]}"` array run included, because bash looks the expanded first word `gh` up as the function.

Seam 2: the ledger trusts whatever login auth-status answers: reconstruct_state and _trusted_set add it to the trusted set, and RationaleReader._identity uses it as `self` and caches it in identity.json; setting forgeAccount moves that login from the default gh login to the account login.

Seam 2: on a change whose settle markers were posted under the old login, the next reconstruct or stateful command raises `unclassified_authors: <old login>` and exits 2 before any write, until the caller adds --trust <old login> (the documented cross-identity resume); the switch parks the settle loop, it does not mis-trust.
Seam 2: rationale notes posted under the old login stop reading as `self` in rationale-read and rank as trusted only through --trust.

Seam 2/4: the identity cache is scoped by git common dir, AFK_CFG_FORGE and remote.origin.url, never by account; after a switch an offline read returns the old cached login (source cache) until a live read overwrites identity.json.
Seam 2: gc-check.sh reads only change-state `merged` through dispatch, and its smoke stub glab answers merged for any argv, so the GITLAB_HOST-only change (b) leaves it unchanged.
Seam 2: the github-issues tracker runs gh outside forge.sh's gh(), so tracker writes would keep the default login while forge writes switch to forgeAccount.

Seam 3: FRESHNESS.md rule 1 needs MANIFEST.md env rows in the same commit for GH_HOST, GH_TOKEN and GITLAB_HOST as the forge scripts set them; MANIFEST.md names GH_TOKEN only for protected-lookup (:1002), and a search for GH_HOST|GH_TOKEN|GITLAB_HOST outside docs/afk found no other MANIFEST row.
Seam 3/4: ADAPTERS.md:100-101 and MANIFEST.md:971 state that each gh or glab call stops at AFK_FORGE_TIMEOUT; a token fetch run outside that limit makes both false.

Seam 3: the review-record lockstep (AGENTS.md:151) and the FRESHNESS.md ledger row bind a trust-rule change to forge_ledger.py, test_forge_ledger.py, the execute, preflight and settle-change callers and the forge adapter contracts and tests in one commit; the auth-status shape {authenticated,user} itself does not change.

Seam 3: documents that go stale under (a): github CONTRACT.md 'Configuration keys read' (forge, github.remote, git.base-branch) and its 'No credential is configured' line, github forge.sh:15, gitlab CONTRACT.md keys list, ADAPTERS.md forge section (no account or host rule); gitlab forge.sh:16-17 'Nothing here reads a token' stays true under (b).

project_from_remote.project() returns only the path after the host (owner/name), never a host, so a helper cannot derive the host through it; protected-lookup derives the host itself with _host_of and `git remote get-url` for insteadOf/include, and afk-config detect_forge is a second host parser

branch_protection.protection() takes forge, branch, repo, cwd, limit, api and host and no account; _login_token asks `gh auth token --hostname github.com` with no --user, so the token is the active github.com account's, and test_protected_lookup.py:654 pins that exact argv

Local gh 2.92.0 help: `gh auth token` has -u/--user and -h/--hostname; `gh api` and `gh issue create` list no --user flag; `gh auth switch` changes the active account in the stored configuration; GH_TOKEN takes precedence over stored credentials and GH_HOST names the host where a command gives none

A per-repository account for `gh issue` and `gh api` calls needs a token in the child environment (GH_TOKEN from `gh auth token --hostname <host> --user <account>`) or a global `gh auth switch` that every concurrent session shares; a helper that returns only host and account therefore leaves each caller to fetch and hold that token, so `never a token` holds for the helper, not for the call path

The guard already reads outside worktree add/move: Judge.verdict() calls lookup() for every identified mutation of a linked worktree on an uncached branch, and lookup() runs the full afk-config load() when any config file exists plus the forge network read capped at min(guard time left, AFK_PROTECTED_TIMEOUT or 5 s)

A helper that reads the personal file or spawns git inside lookup() adds that cost to every guard verdict, against the locked L4 rule; the cheap path is to take the account from the load() that _configured() already runs (but that merge includes ~/.afk) and to add --user to the one existing `gh auth token` spawn on the public-API no-env-token path, so the spawn count stays 1

Rules the new path must keep: a login token goes only to the public API (branch_protection.py:177-182, :190; test :657); 401/403 drops the token answers and retries through the CLI (:203-204; test :523); a host the CLI has no login for is an error, never a default-host read (:160-174, :209, :278; tests :743-746); SSH aliases resolve through ssh -G (:153-157; tests :749-764); a spawn needs 0.3 s of budget left (:190); the cache key holds no account (protected-lookup.py:223)
